# 1. What the Research Found

**MONITORING. Re-check window: the UK-MaRes hub's programme milestones through its 31st March 2027 end date, and any published output from the Events Environmental Sustainability Platform project.**

This item profiles Cranfield University's Centre for Logistics, Procurement and Supply Chain Management, focusing on two active projects directly relevant to the workspace: the UK national clean Maritime Research (UK-MaRes) hub, and a Novel Events Environmental Sustainability Platform.

FACT: "Article: Cranfield University part of a new £21.3m national research hub to decarbonise the UK maritime sector." *Source: Cranfield University news article on the UK-MaRes hub, cited on the UK-MaRes project page. https://www.cranfield.ac.uk/som/research-projects/uk-national-clean-maritime-research-hub

FACT: "Led by Durham University and in collaboration with 12 other universities, this project will establish the UK national clean Maritime Research (UK-MaRes) hub to deliver a disruptive programme of activity that will accelerate the decarbonisation and elimination of harmful air pollution for the maritime sector." *Source: UK national clean Maritime Research Hub, Cranfield University. https://www.cranfield.ac.uk/som/research-projects/uk-national-clean-maritime-research-hub

FACT: "Dates 1st September 2023 to 31st March 2027 Sponsor EPSRC and Department for Transport Funded £345,496 out of £7.4m (total value of the project)" *Source: UK national clean Maritime Research Hub, Cranfield University. https://www.cranfield.ac.uk/som/research-projects/uk-national-clean-maritime-research-hub

FACT: "the hub also aims to feed into a clean maritime strategy that can adapt to place-based challenges and provide targeted technical and socio-economic interventions through a novel co-innovation methodology." *Source: UK national clean Maritime Research Hub, Cranfield University. https://www.cranfield.ac.uk/som/research-projects/uk-national-clean-maritime-research-hub

FACT: "Partners University of Durham, University of Liverpool, City University, University of Birmingham, University of Sheffield, University of St Andrews, University of Ulster, University of Brighton, University of Aston, University of Newcastle, the Port of Felixstowe, the Port of Dover, Peel Ports, Cosco Shipping (UK), DFDS, MOL Group, Freeport East, Rux Energy, and many more." *Source: UK national clean Maritime Research Hub, Cranfield University. https://www.cranfield.ac.uk/som/research-projects/uk-national-clean-maritime-research-hub

FACT: "A Novel Events Environmental Sustainability Platform This project will develop a novel Events Environmental Sustainability Platform to help events management companies and their clients verify their Greenhouse Gas emissions, and to make recommendations on how to reduce event related GHG emissions." *Source: Research projects (current and past), Centre for Logistics, Procurement and Supply Chain Management, Cranfield University. https://www.cranfield.ac.uk/som/research-centres/centre-for-logistics-procurement-and-supply-chain-management/research-projects-current-and-past

FACT: "Reverse Logistics in Circular Economy The project will provide clear strategies to enable effective supply chain of servitised products by developing the reverse logistics process based on the circular economy principles." *Source: Research projects (current and past), Cranfield University. https://www.cranfield.ac.uk/som/research-centres/centre-for-logistics-procurement-and-supply-chain-management/research-projects-current-and-past

FACT: "Our research interests are in the areas of agile and lean supply chains, procurement, interorganisational relationships, supply chain strategy, decision support systems, information systems, sustainability and circular economy, food and retail supply chains, simulation and modelling, and manufacturing supply chain." *Source: Centre for Logistics, Procurement and Supply Chain Management, Cranfield University. https://www.cranfield.ac.uk/som/research-centres/centre-for-logistics-procurement-and-supply-chain-management

FACT: "Our academic colleagues are actively publishing in top ranked logistics and supply chain management journals and are members of numerous editorial boards. They are also developing international thought leadership profiles in their particular fields." *Source: Centre for Logistics, Procurement and Supply Chain Management, Cranfield University. https://www.cranfield.ac.uk/som/research-centres/centre-for-logistics-procurement-and-supply-chain-management

# 2. Why This Finding Matters Operationally and Commercially

FACT: "Partners University of Durham, University of Liverpool, City University, University of Birmingham, University of Sheffield, University of St Andrews, University of Ulster, University of Brighton, University of Aston, University of Newcastle, the Port of Felixstowe, the Port of Dover, Peel Ports, Cosco Shipping (UK), DFDS, MOL Group, Freeport East, Rux Energy, and many more." *Source: UK national clean Maritime Research Hub, Cranfield University. https://www.cranfield.ac.uk/som/research-projects/uk-national-clean-maritime-research-hub

*Operational implication:* the UK-MaRes hub's partner list names the Port of Felixstowe, the Port of Dover, Peel Ports, Cosco Shipping (UK), DFDS, and MOL Group directly -- ports and carriers a workspace routing UK ocean freight is likely to already touch. A hub output affecting one of these named partners is directly relevant to the workspace's own UK gateway choices, not a generic academic finding.

FACT: "A Novel Events Environmental Sustainability Platform This project will develop a novel Events Environmental Sustainability Platform to help events management companies and their clients verify their Greenhouse Gas emissions, and to make recommendations on how to reduce event related GHG emissions." *Source: Research projects (current and past), Cranfield University. https://www.cranfield.ac.uk/som/research-centres/centre-for-logistics-procurement-and-supply-chain-management/research-projects-current-and-past

*Operational implication:* an Events Environmental Sustainability Platform aimed at helping events-management companies and their clients verify and reduce GHG emissions is directly relevant to the workspace's own live-events cargo vertical; the workspace should monitor this project for a client-facing GHG verification tool it could reference or adopt.

FACT: "Project SCALE (Step Change in Agri-Food Ecosystems) aimed to increase economic competitiveness but, as importantly, to also improve environmental and social sustainability of food and drink supply chain logistics across North-West Europe." *Source: Project SCALE case study, Cranfield University. https://www.cranfield.ac.uk/som/case-studies/project-scale

FACT: "We were the lead partner in the three-year project which involved other research institutions (University of Artois and Wageningen University), working in collaboration with DHL and European Food and Farming Partnerships (EFFP)." *Source: Project SCALE case study, Cranfield University. https://www.cranfield.ac.uk/som/case-studies/project-scale

*Analytical inference:* Project SCALE's own DHL collaboration on food and drink supply chain sustainability across North-West Europe is evidence that a major global logistics operator has already partnered with Cranfield on comparable sustainability research; this is a credibility signal for the workspace when citing Cranfield's work in a client conversation.

FACT: "We identified three key building blocks which are needed for businesses to make a meaningful step change in their approach to supply chain sustainability – belief that improving the TBL can really improve competitiveness and profitability; recognition that progress in this area is not easy and that certain core enablers must be in place to drive real change; and articulation of a compelling TBL value proposition with an action plan for implementation." *Source: Project SCALE case study, Cranfield University. https://www.cranfield.ac.uk/som/case-studies/project-scale

# 3. What the Finding Changes for Strategy, Claims, or Decisions

**1. A specific, named GHG-verification tool for the events vertical may be forthcoming.**

*Analytical inference:* because the Events Environmental Sustainability Platform is explicitly aimed at helping events-management companies and their clients verify and reduce GHG emissions, the workspace's live-events cargo practice should track this project's progress as a potential future client-facing tool or methodology reference, rather than treat event-logistics GHG verification as an unaddressed research gap.

**2. UK-MaRes hub partners are a specific, checkable list against the workspace's own UK gateway ports and carriers.**

*Analytical inference:* the workspace should cross-check its own current UK ocean-gateway ports and carrier relationships (Felixstowe, Dover, Peel Ports facilities, Cosco, DFDS, MOL) against the UK-MaRes partner list; a workspace already routing through a listed partner has a more direct line to any decarbonisation intervention the hub develops than one routing through a non-partner port.

**3. Cranfield's SCALE framework (three building blocks) is a citable structure for client sustainability-strategy conversations, not a road-freight-specific tool.**

*Analytical inference:* SCALE's own three building blocks (the belief that improving triple-bottom-line performance improves competitiveness; recognising core enablers must be in place; articulating a compelling value proposition with an implementation plan) is a general supply-chain-sustainability framework developed for food and drink logistics, not built for freight forwarding specifically; it is citable as a structuring device for a client conversation, not as freight-specific guidance.

# 4. Client Conversation Talking Points and Public Position

**What the workspace can credibly say:**

- "Cranfield University leads UK research directly relevant to our operations: the £21.3m UK-MaRes national maritime decarbonisation hub (partnered with the Port of Felixstowe, Port of Dover, Peel Ports, Cosco, DFDS and MOL Group, running to 31st March 2027) and a new Events Environmental Sustainability Platform aimed at helping events companies verify and reduce GHG emissions."
- "Cranfield's Project SCALE, run in partnership with DHL across North-West Europe's food and drink supply chains, identified three building blocks needed for a business to make a genuine step change in supply chain sustainability."

**Pitfalls to avoid:**

- Do not cite specific quantitative results (emissions reductions, cost savings, or efficiency gains) from Project SCALE; the captured pool describes the project's aim and method but does not report its quantitative outcomes.
- Do not present the UK-MaRes hub's findings as already informing UK Department for Transport regulation; the hub runs through 31st March 2027 and no formal regulatory consultation trigger is established in the captured pool.
- Do not present the Events Environmental Sustainability Platform as already deployed; the captured pool describes it as a project "to develop" the platform, not a completed, deployed tool.

# 5. What the Finding Does Not Resolve

GAP: Whether UK-MaRes hub findings will trigger a formal Department for Transport regulatory consultation before the hub's 2027 end date is not established by the captured pool.

GAP: SCALE's quantitative results, specific emissions reductions, cost savings, or efficiency gains achieved, are not stated in the captured pool.

GAP: The Events Environmental Sustainability Platform's deployment status, including development phase, partner companies, or a completion date, is not available from the captured pool.

GAP: The Centre's active research portfolio, as captured, does not surface projects specifically addressing aviation emissions, sustainable aviation fuel, truck CO2 standards, urban clean-air zones, or zero-emission-vehicle requirements.

# 1. Operational Cost Baseline for the Region

This profile synthesises current intelligence on the operational and infrastructure-investment environment for freight-forwarding and logistics operations in Brazil. It is written for workspaces whose primary transport mode is ocean, with road and air as secondary/tertiary, operating across high-value and time-sensitive cargo verticals, with Brazilian gateways serving primarily South American and transatlantic trade lanes.

The captured pool for this item is dominated by Brazilian government-portal navigation structure (the ANTT road-transport regulator, the ANP oil and gas regulator, ANEEL the electricity regulator, the Diario Oficial federal register, and the Senate) rather than article or dataset content; the one substantive capture is an ANTT news article on national transport-infrastructure investment, reproduced here in its own Portuguese with labelled English analysis (Section 6).

FACT: "Na FIESP, ANTT apresenta carteira de R$ 300 bilhões e reforça segurança para investimentos em infraestrutura no Brasil" *Source: ANTT (Agencia Nacional de Transportes Terrestres) news article, published 15/04/2026. https://www.gov.br/antt/pt-br/assuntos/ultimas-noticias/na-fiesp-antt-apresenta-carteira-de-r-300-bilhoes-e-reforca-seguranca-para-investimentos-em-infraestrutura-no-brasil

FACT: "Hoje, o país conta com mais de 18 mil quilômetros de rodovias concedidas, com previsão de R$ 306 bilhões em investimentos (CAPEX) e R$ 219 bilhões destinados à operação e manutenção (OPEX)." *Source: ANTT news article. https://www.gov.br/antt/pt-br/assuntos/ultimas-noticias/na-fiesp-antt-apresenta-carteira-de-r-300-bilhoes-e-reforca-seguranca-para-investimentos-em-infraestrutura-no-brasil

*Per the workspace's reading:* this states a national CAPEX/OPEX envelope for Brazil's concessioned road network, not a per-shipment or per-lane operational cost the workspace can quote directly; it is the closest cost-scale signal the captured pool provides for Brazilian road infrastructure.

FACT: "No setor ferroviário, são 15 mil quilômetros operacionais, além de novos projetos estruturantes e ampliações em curso." *Source: ANTT news article. https://www.gov.br/antt/pt-br/assuntos/ultimas-noticias/na-fiesp-antt-apresenta-carteira-de-r-300-bilhoes-e-reforca-seguranca-para-investimentos-em-infraestrutura-no-brasil

FACT: "Atualmente, o setor ferroviário soma mais de R$ 227 bilhões em novos aportes, com milhares de quilômetros autorizados e dezenas de contratos vigentes." *Source: ANTT news article. https://www.gov.br/antt/pt-br/assuntos/ultimas-noticias/na-fiesp-antt-apresenta-carteira-de-r-300-bilhoes-e-reforca-seguranca-para-investimentos-em-infraestrutura-no-brasil

**Industrial electricity and fuel pricing.**

*No content for this section as of the export date: current industrial electricity tariff rates or fuel (diesel/bunker) pump prices for Brazil are not available from the captured source blocks. The ANEEL (electricity regulator) and ANP (oil and gas regulator) captures both returned only site-navigation structure, not tariff or price data; the ANEEL capture additionally carries a character-encoding defect (mojibake) in the small amount of body text it does contain, which is not reproduced here as a verbatim quote because it cannot be confirmed to be readable, undistorted source text.*

# 2. Feasibility of Specific Operational Choices

FACT: "No setor ferroviário, a agenda inclui novos leilões, renovações contratuais e projetos estratégicos, como a Ferrogrão e a EF-118, além da ampliação da malha existente." *Source: ANTT news article. https://www.gov.br/antt/pt-br/assuntos/ultimas-noticias/na-fiesp-antt-apresenta-carteira-de-r-300-bilhoes-e-reforca-seguranca-para-investimentos-em-infraestrutura-no-brasil

*Analytical inference:* the explicit naming of Ferrogrão and EF-118 as strategic rail projects alongside new auctions and contract renewals signals that rail-freight capacity expansion is an active national policy priority in Brazil, relevant to a workspace evaluating rail as a modal option for Brazilian inland corridors; the captured pool does not give a specific completion date, route capacity, or tariff for either named project (Section 5).

*No content for this section as of the export date: specific feasibility data for EV or alternative-fuel road-fleet adoption, warehouse retrofit costs, or port-side decarbonisation infrastructure in Brazil is not available from the captured source blocks.*

# 3. Cost Comparison Against Alternatives

*No content for this section as of the export date: specific numerical breakeven or payback data comparing operational choices (rail vs road, owned vs leased fleet, or any other alternative) in the Brazilian context are not available from the sourced blocks. This section is replaced by this honest note rather than filled with invented figures.*

# 4. Cross-Regional Strategic Implications

*No content for this section as of the export date: Cross-Regional Strategic Implications is a MATRIX-then-transitive comparison requiring the same cost or feasibility dimension sourced across at least two of the workspace's active regions. This record's stored pool covers only Brazil; no other regional_data item's sourced figures were supplied for this authoring pass, so no cross-regional comparison can be proven from this single stored pool. This omission will resolve once a second active region reaches sourced coverage on the same cost/feasibility dimensions.*

# 5. Competitive Positioning in the Region

*No content for this section as of the export date: named-competitor sustainability positioning or certification data for freight operators in Brazil is not available from the captured source blocks, which consist of Brazilian government-portal navigation structure and one national-infrastructure news article rather than any operator's own published material.*

# 6. Client Conversation Talking Points

**What the workspace can credibly say:**

- *Per the workspace's reading:* Brazil's federal road-transport regulator (ANTT) has publicly presented a national investment pipeline of over BRL 300 billion (BRL 306 billion in planned road CAPEX plus BRL 219 billion in OPEX for the concessioned highway network alone), signalling sustained multi-year investment in the country's road and rail freight infrastructure.
- *Per the workspace's reading:* named strategic rail projects (Ferrogrão, EF-118) are part of the government's active 2026 agenda, relevant context for a client asking about future Brazilian rail-freight modal options, though the captured pool gives no completion timeline for either.

**What the workspace should not claim without verification:**

- Do not present the BRL 300+ billion investment figures as current operating costs or freight rates; they are national infrastructure CAPEX/OPEX and auction totals, not per-shipment or per-lane costs.
- Do not claim a specific Brazilian industrial electricity tariff or fuel price; the captured pool does not carry this data (Section 1).

**Questions the workspace can pose to clients:**

- "For Brazilian inland corridors, is your routing currently entirely road-based, or would a rail option become relevant once the Ferrogrão or EF-118 projects the government has flagged reach operational status?"

*Analytical inference:* these talking points draw only on the FACT and GAP claims already established in Sections 1 and 2 above; no new fact is introduced in this section.

# 7. Pending Changes That Shift the Calculus

### MONITORING

FACT: "Entre 2023 e 2025, foram realizados 19 leilões rodoviários, totalizando mais de 7 mil quilômetros concedidos e cerca de R$ 230 bilhões em investimentos." *Source: ANTT news article. https://www.gov.br/antt/pt-br/assuntos/ultimas-noticias/na-fiesp-antt-apresenta-carteira-de-r-300-bilhoes-e-reforca-seguranca-para-investimentos-em-infraestrutura-no-brasil

FACT: "Para 2026, estão previstos novos leilões que somam mais de 3.200 quilômetros e R$ 71,6 bilhões." *Source: ANTT news article. https://www.gov.br/antt/pt-br/assuntos/ultimas-noticias/na-fiesp-antt-apresenta-carteira-de-r-300-bilhoes-e-reforca-seguranca-para-investimentos-em-infraestrutura-no-brasil

*Operational implication:* the 2026 road-auction pipeline quoted above is a near-term signal for the workspace to monitor for new concessioned road corridors that could affect routing options or tolling on Brazilian lanes it uses.

FACT: "A expectativa é de geração de mais de 1,5 milhão de empregos, entre diretos, indiretos e efeito renda, além da melhoria da segurança viária, redução de custos logísticos e aumento da competitividade nacional." *Source: ANTT news article. https://www.gov.br/antt/pt-br/assuntos/ultimas-noticias/na-fiesp-antt-apresenta-carteira-de-r-300-bilhoes-e-reforca-seguranca-para-investimentos-em-infraestrutura-no-brasil

*Analytical inference:* the government's own stated expectation (over 1.5 million jobs, plus reduced logistics costs and increased national competitiveness) is a policy framing claim from the regulator itself, not an independently verified outcome; cited here as the government's own stated rationale for the investment programme, not as an established fact about logistics-cost reduction.

- 2023 to 2025: 19 road-concession auctions completed in Brazil (figures quoted in Section 7 above).
- 2026: new road auctions planned (figures quoted in Section 7 above); the government's rail-sector agenda for the year includes new auctions, contract renewals, and the Ferrogrão and EF-118 strategic projects.
- 15/04/2026: date of the ANTT news article this profile is grounded on.

# 1. Operational Cost Baseline for the Region

This profile synthesises current intelligence on operational costs, regulatory environment, infrastructure feasibility, and the road-freight decarbonisation landscape for freight-forwarding and logistics operations in India. It is written for workspaces whose primary transport mode is ocean, with air and road as secondary, operating across high-value and time-sensitive cargo verticals, with India serving Asia-Europe and Asia-Americas trade lanes plus significant domestic road-freight legs.

FACT: "Transport accounts for 14% of India’s GHG emissions, with medium and heavy-duty trucks responsible for 44% of that share—despite comprising just 3% of vehicles on the road." *Source: "India's Transport Transformation: Three Policies to Shape the Road Ahead," ICCT. https://theicct.org/indias-transport-transformation-three-policies-to-shape-the-road-ahead-sep25/

FACT: "India’s logistics costs, at about 13% of GDP, far exceed the global average." *Source: ICCT. https://theicct.org/indias-transport-transformation-three-policies-to-shape-the-road-ahead-sep25/

FACT: "With 70% of freight moving by road and fuel making up a large portion of costs, electrifying trucks is both an environmental and economic imperative." *Source: ICCT. https://theicct.org/indias-transport-transformation-three-policies-to-shape-the-road-ahead-sep25/

FACT: "Logistics costs remain high, with companies spending 10–15% of their expenses on transporting goods to and from factories." *Source: "Accelerating India's Freight Decarbonization," WRI India. https://wri-india.org/initiatives/accelerating-indias-freight-decarbonization

*Per the workspace's reading:* both sources independently confirm road freight's outsized cost and emissions footprint in India (70% of freight by road per ICCT; 10-15% of a shipping company's own expenses spent on transport per WRI India), which is the structural reason road-fleet decarbonisation and cost pressure are linked issues for a workspace's Indian road legs, not separate topics.

FACT: "The high upfront cost of electric trucks, coupled with limited charging infrastructure, remains a significant roadblock." *Source: WRI India. https://wri-india.org/initiatives/accelerating-indias-freight-decarbonization

**Industrial electricity and fuel pricing.**

GAP: Specific current diesel retail price (INR/litre, national average) is not available from primary sources as of 2026-09-17.

GAP: Specific total-cost-of-ownership breakeven or payback period figures for electric versus diesel trucks in India are not available from primary sources as of 2026-09-17.

# 2. Feasibility of Specific Operational Choices

FACT: "India has only 869 electric medium- and heavy-duty freight vehicles." *Source: WRI India. https://wri-india.org/initiatives/accelerating-indias-freight-decarbonization

*Per the workspace's reading:* fewer than 900 electric medium- and heavy-duty freight vehicles in service nationally is a very small base relative to India's overall truck fleet; electric road-freight capacity is not yet a scaled operational option for the workspace's Indian road legs.

FACT: "In July 2025, the Ministry of Heavy Industries released guidelines for electric trucks under the PM e-DRIVE scheme." *Source: ICCT. https://theicct.org/indias-transport-transformation-three-policies-to-shape-the-road-ahead-sep25/

FACT: "By supporting electric trucks, e-DRIVE addresses three challenges at once: Reducing logistics costs through lower fuel dependency. Strengthening domestic manufacturing of advanced EV technologies such as heavy-duty batteries and charging systems. # 1. Operational Cost Baseline for the Region

This item's title names IEA electricity price data for large industrial customers (2019-2024); every one of the six IEA captures in this item's stored pool, and the European Commission's finance-portal homepage, returned only a Cloudflare security-verification interstitial or a bare language-selection page (Section 8), so none of them grounds any claim below. The one real-content capture in this pool is Eurostat's own Electricity Price Statistics article, which is EU-wide (not IEA-sourced) and reports household and non-household (not specifically large-industrial) price bands. This profile is authored as an EU electricity-cost baseline on that basis; the specific IEA large-industrial-customer comparison the title names is a genuine GAP (Section 5), not silently substituted.

FACT: "electricity prices in the second half of 2025 were highest in Ireland (€0.2552 per kWh), Cyprus (€0.2429 per kWh) and Germany(€0.2264 per kWh). The lowest prices were observed in Finland (€0.0748 per kWh) and Sweden (€0.0970 per kWh). The EU average price in the second half of 2025 was €0.1837 per kWh." *Source: Electricity Price Statistics, Eurostat (European Commission). https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/statistics-explained/index.php?title=Electricity_price_statistics

*Per the workspace's reading:* non-household electricity prices (the closest band in this pool to a commercial/logistics-facility rate, though not specifically the large-industrial-customer band the item title names) show an over 3x spread across EU member states in H2 2025 (figures quoted above, Finland lowest and Ireland highest) -- a workspace with facilities or subcontractors in multiple EU countries should expect materially different electricity cost exposure by country, not a single EU-wide rate.

FACT: "Non-household electricity prices in the EU were highest in Ireland (€0.2552 per kWh) and lowest in Finland (€0.0748 per kWh) in the second half of 2025." *Source: Eurostat. https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/statistics-explained/index.php?title=Electricity_price_statistics

FACT: "Electricity prices for non-household consumers in the EU fell by 5.4% in the second half of 2025 compared to the same period in 2024 and by 3.5% from the first half of 2025." *Source: Eurostat. https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/statistics-explained/index.php?title=Electricity_price_statistics

FACT: "The EU average price in the second half of 2025 – a weighted average using the most recent (2024) consumption data for electricity by household consumers – was €0.2896 per kWh." *Source: Eurostat. https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/statistics-explained/index.php?title=Electricity_price_statistics

FACT: "reaching €0.2075 per kWh in the first half and €0.2059 per kWh in the second half." *Source: Eurostat. https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/statistics-explained/index.php?title=Electricity_price_statistics

FACT: "The average share of total taxes and levies at EU level in the second half of 2025 was 28.9%" *Source: Eurostat. https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/statistics-explained/index.php?title=Electricity_price_statistics

FACT: "electricity prices in the second half of 2025 were highest in Ireland (€0.4042 per kWh), Germany (€0.3869 per kWh), Belgium (€0.3499 per kWh), and Denmark (€0.3312 per kWh)" *Source: Eurostat. https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/statistics-explained/index.php?title=Electricity_price_statistics

FACT: "The price without taxes, i.e. the energy, supply and network, was relatively stable between 2016 and 2020. The prices rose sharply in both semesters of 2022 and reached a peak of €0.2385 per kWh in the first half of 2023." *Source: Eurostat. https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/statistics-explained/index.php?title=Electricity_price_statistics

FACT: "500 MWh" *Source: Eurostat (the article's own annual consumption band definition for the non-household price series quoted above). https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/statistics-explained/index.php?title=Electricity_price_statistics

*Analytical inference:* the non-household consumption band this Eurostat series reports on (the annual consumption band quoted above) is a mid-size commercial/industrial band; it is not confirmed to be the same "large industrial customer" band the IEA data the item's own title names would report, so the figures above should be read as an EU commercial-electricity baseline, not a direct substitute for large-industrial-customer pricing specifically.

GAP: IEA finding that EU industrial electricity prices are approximately double US levels is not span-groundable from the available blocks; every IEA capture in this pool returned a Cloudflare security-verification page, not article or chart content.

# 2. Feasibility of Specific Operational Choices

This section is replaced by this honest note rather than filled with invented figures.*

*No content for this section as of the export date: Cross-Regional Strategic Implications is a MATRIX-then-transitive comparison requiring the same cost or feasibility dimension sourced across at least two of the workspace's active regions. This record's stored pool covers only the EU electricity market; no other regional_data item's sourced figures were supplied for this authoring pass, so no cross-regional comparison (EU vs US, EU vs China) can be proven from this single stored pool, even though the item's own prior draft flagged exactly this comparison as the point of interest. This omission will resolve once a second active region reaches sourced coverage on the same cost dimension.*

# 6. Client Conversation Talking Points

**What the workspace can credibly say:**

- *Per the workspace's reading:* non-household electricity prices across EU member states in H2 2025 showed an over threefold spread between the lowest (Finland) and highest (Ireland) countries (figures quoted in Section 1); a client asking about EU facility siting or subcontractor selection should be told this variation is real and material, not a single "EU rate."
- *Per the workspace's reading:* non-household EU electricity prices fell 5.4% year-on-year in H2 2025, a easing signal after the 2022-2023 price spike Eurostat's own household series also documents.

**What the workspace should not claim without verification:**

- Do not present the Eurostat non-household price band as the same "large industrial customer" band the IEA reports on; this pool could not access IEA's own large-industrial-customer data, and the two bands are not confirmed equivalent.
- Do not cite a specific EU-vs-US or EU-vs-China electricity price ratio; the IEA sources that would ground such a comparison were inaccessible in this capture (Section 1).

*Analytical inference:* these talking points draw only on the FACT and GAP claims already established in Section 1 above; no new fact is introduced in this section.

*Operational implication:* Eurostat's own planned update date is the next point at which H1 2026 non-household price data becomes available; the workspace's own next monitoring pass on EU electricity costs should target that date rather than an earlier re-check.

GAP: EU ETS Phase 4 tightening (2026-2030) and free-allocation contraction are pending changes that could materially shift EU electricity and carbon-cost comparisons; this is not span-groundable from the available blocks in this pool.

# 1. Operational Cost Baseline for the Region

This profile synthesises current intelligence on energy costs, market conditions, and the road-freight electrification trend for freight-forwarding and logistics operations in the EU. It is written for workspaces whose primary transport mode is ocean, with air and road as secondary, operating across high-value and time-sensitive cargo verticals, with EU core-market gateways serving intra-European and transatlantic/Asia trade lanes.

FACT: "The EU quarterly gas and electricity market reports analyse market data in detail to examine trends and challenges." *Source: European Commission DG ENER, Market Analysis quarterly reports. https://energy.ec.europa.eu/data-and-analysis/market-analysis_en

FACT: "The 6th report on energy prices and costs  was published in February 2025." *Source: European Commission DG ENER, Energy Prices and Costs in Europe. https://energy.ec.europa.eu/data-and-analysis/energy-prices-and-costs-europe_en

FACT: "although the EU’s energy import bill receded to €427 billion in 2024 (after reaching the peak of €604 billion in 2022), is still a significant drain on the European economy." *Source: European Commission DG ENER, Energy Prices and Costs in Europe (6th report). https://energy.ec.europa.eu/data-and-analysis/energy-prices-and-costs-europe_en

FACT: "industrial gas and electricity prices, while lower than during the crisis, are still 2-4 times higher than in the EU’s main trading partners, which threatens the long-term competitiveness of European industry." *Source: European Commission DG ENER, Energy Prices and Costs in Europe. https://energy.ec.europa.eu/data-and-analysis/energy-prices-and-costs-europe_en

*Operational implication:* the Commission's own finding that EU industrial gas and electricity prices remain 2-4x higher than in the EU's main trading partners is a direct, structural cost disadvantage for any EU-based logistics or warehousing facility relative to non-EU competitors; this is the single most material cost-baseline fact in this profile for a workspace evaluating EU facility investment.

FACT: "due notably to the time lag in transmission of prices between the two market segments, the drop in wholesale prices is yet to bring down retail energy prices , which are still higher for households and enterprises than before 2021." *Source: European Commission DG ENER. https://energy.ec.europa.eu/data-and-analysis/energy-prices-and-costs-europe_en

FACT: "Household gas prices were almost twice as high in 2023 than before the crisis." *Source: European Commission DG ENER. https://energy.ec.europa.eu/data-and-analysis/energy-prices-and-costs-europe_en

FACT: "Wholesale prices have stabilised on both electricity and gas markets since the energy crisis of 2021-2023, although at a level higher than their historical averages." *Source: European Commission DG ENER. https://energy.ec.europa.eu/data-and-analysis/energy-prices-and-costs-europe_en

FACT: "European wholesale prices averaged 35 €/MWh in the second quarter of 2025, a significant decrease of 24% compared to the previous quarter and a 10% increase year-on-year." *Source: European Commission DG ENER, EU gas market report Q2 2025. https://energy.ec.europa.eu/data-and-analysis/market-analysis_en

FACT: "Retail gas prices decreased by 2% compared to the previous quarter and increased by 9% year-on-year. The EU quarterly average retail price was 110 €/MWh." *Source: European Commission DG ENER, EU gas market report Q2 2025. https://energy.ec.europa.eu/data-and-analysis/market-analysis_en

FACT: "Retail electricity prices for households in EU capital cities rose marginally by 3% in Q2 2025 (to 246 €/MWh)." *Source: European Commission DG ENER, EU electricity market report Q2 2025. https://energy.ec.europa.eu/data-and-analysis/market-analysis_en

FACT: "Additionally, there was significant variation between EU countries with several seeing double-digit percentage increases (e.g. Austria, Luxembourg, Poland) and others seeing large decreases in retail prices due to lower energy costs (e.g. Slovenia, Estonia, France)." *Source: European Commission DG ENER. https://energy.ec.europa.eu/data-and-analysis/market-analysis_en

*Per the workspace's reading:* EU retail electricity prices are not uniform across member states (Austria, Luxembourg and Poland saw double-digit increases in Q2 2025 while Slovenia, Estonia and France saw large decreases); a workspace evaluating EU facility siting should treat this as country-level variation, not a single "EU electricity price."

GAP: Country-level commercial/industrial electricity rates by EU Member State are not available from primary sources as of 2026-09-17.

# 2. Feasibility of Specific Operational Choices

FACT: "Finally, with over 720 000 new electric vehicles sold in Q2 2025, the quarter set an all-time record for sales of EVs in the passenger car segment in the EU - a yearly increase of almost 30% compared with Q2 2024." *Source: European Commission DG ENER, EU electricity market report Q2 2025. https://energy.ec.europa.eu/data-and-analysis/market-analysis_en

FACT: "This translates into a 23% EV share in the EU passenger car market, more than two times the market share registered in the United States (10%)." *Source: European Commission DG ENER. https://energy.ec.europa.eu/data-and-analysis/market-analysis_en

*Analytical inference:* an EU passenger-car EV share more than double the US share (23% versus 10%) is not a direct read on freight-vehicle electrification, but it does indicate the charging-infrastructure and public-policy environment supporting electrification is materially more advanced in EU core markets than in some other regions -- context relevant when a client asks why the workspace treats EU road-fleet electrification differently from other regions.

FACT: "The electricity market report   Q2 2025   confirms that solar generation rose to a new record high for a second quarter, reaching 98 TWh (+20%)." *Source: European Commission DG ENER, EU electricity market report Q2 2025. https://energy.ec.europa.eu/data-and-analysis/market-analysis_en

FACT: "The share of renewables stayed stable at 52% in Q2 2025 (same as in Q2 2024), while the share of fossil fuels rose very slightly to 25% (from 24% in Q2 2024)." *Source: European Commission DG ENER. https://energy.ec.europa.eu/data-and-analysis/market-analysis_en

FACT: "Electricity consumption in the EU stayed flat (+0.4%) compared with Q2 2024." *Source: European Commission DG ENER. https://energy.ec.europa.eu/data-and-analysis/market-analysis_en

GAP: Specific feasibility data, permitting requirements, or grid connection lead times for on-site solar and battery energy storage systems (BESS) at EU logistics facilities are not available from primary sources as of 2026-09-17.

# 3. Cost Comparison Against Alternatives

*No content for this section as of 2026-09-17: specific numerical breakeven or payback data for on-site solar vs grid power, or EV vs diesel road-fleet total cost of ownership specific to freight trucking, in the EU context are not available from the sourced blocks. This section is replaced by this honest note rather than filled with invented figures.*

*No content for this section as of 2026-09-17: Cross-Regional Strategic Implications is a MATRIX-then-transitive comparison requiring the same cost or feasibility dimension sourced across at least two of the workspace's active regions. This record's stored pool covers only the EU; no other regional_data item's sourced figures were supplied for this authoring pass, so no cross-regional comparison can be proven from this single stored pool, even though the Commission's own 2-4x industrial-price finding above (Section 1) names EXACTLY the kind of cross-regional comparison this section would make once a second region's sourced figures are available. This omission will resolve once a second active region reaches sourced coverage on the same cost dimension.*

# 5. Competitive Positioning in the Region

*No content for this section as of 2026-09-17: named-competitor sustainability or energy-sourcing positioning data for freight operators in the EU is not available from the captured source blocks, which consist of European Commission market-analysis pages rather than any operator's own published material.*

# 6. Client Conversation Talking Points

**What the workspace can credibly say:**

- *Per the workspace's reading:* the European Commission's own analysis finds EU industrial gas and electricity prices are still 2-4 times higher than in the EU's main trading partners, a structural competitiveness factor for any EU-based logistics operation, not a temporary condition.
- *Per the workspace's reading:* the EU's energy import bill eased from its 2022 peak by 2024 (figures quoted in Section 1), but the Commission itself still calls it "a significant drain on the European economy" -- useful context for why EU energy-cost pressure, while easing, has not resolved.
- *Per the workspace's reading:* EV sales in the EU passenger-car segment hit an all-time quarterly record in Q2 2025 (over 720,000 vehicles, 23% market share), more than double the US market share, evidence the EU's charging and policy environment for electrification is comparatively mature.

**What the workspace should not claim without verification:**

- Do not present a single "EU electricity price"; retail electricity price movement varies materially by member state (Section 1).
- Do not extrapolate the EU's strong passenger-car EV adoption to heavy-duty freight trucking; the captured pool's EV figures are for the passenger-car segment specifically.

*Analytical inference:* these talking points draw only on the FACT and GAP claims already established in Sections 1 and 2 above; no new fact is introduced in this section.

# 7. Pending Changes That Shift the Calculus

### MONITORING

GAP: The ETS2 emissions trading scheme is scheduled to extend to cover road transport fuel in a future compliance phase, adding a carbon-cost layer to diesel and LNG road-freight fuel; the specific per-tonne carbon cost for road freight is not available from primary sources as of 2026-09-17.

FACT: "The share of LNG in overall EU gas supply further increased to 46%. Pipeline gas supply from Russia halved year-on-year and decreased by 15% compared to the previous quarter." *Source: European Commission DG ENER, EU gas market report Q2 2025. https://energy.ec.europa.eu/data-and-analysis/market-analysis_en

FACT: "The U.S. has become the second largest EU gas supplier with 27%, next to Norway, which kept its number one position by 30%." *Source: European Commission DG ENER. https://energy.ec.europa.eu/data-and-analysis/market-analysis_en

FACT: "Russia’s share in overall EU gas supplied declined to 12% by 6 percentage points year-on-year." *Source: European Commission DG ENER, EU gas market report Q2 2025. https://energy.ec.europa.eu/data-and-analysis/market-analysis_en

*Operational implication:* the continued structural shift of EU gas supply away from Russia (down to a 12% share) and toward LNG (46% of supply, led by the US) is the underlying driver of the price volatility and elevated levels described in Section 1; the workspace should track this diversification trend as the leading indicator for future EU energy-cost direction, not treat current prices as a stable baseline.

- February 2025: the European Commission published its 6th report on Energy Prices and Costs in Europe.
- Q2 2025: the reporting quarter for the gas and electricity market data quoted throughout this profile.

entries.body:
# 1. Operational Cost Baseline for the Region

This profile synthesises current intelligence on freight planning, permitting, and the regulatory environment for freight-forwarding and logistics operations in Iowa. It is written for workspaces whose primary transport mode is road, with rail as a secondary modal consideration, operating across time-sensitive and multimodal cargo verticals, with Iowa serving as a pass-through and origin/destination state for US Midwest freight lanes.

FACT: "Official State of Iowa Website" *Source: Iowa DOT, Freight Planning. https://iowadot.gov/transportation-development/systems-planning/areas-planning/freight

FACT: "a significant amount of freight originates outside of Iowa and moves though the state to destinations in other states." *Source: Iowa DOT, Freight Planning. https://iowadot.gov/transportation-development/systems-planning/areas-planning/freight

*Operational implication:* the Iowa DOT's own framing (a significant share of freight through Iowa originates elsewhere and continues to other states) confirms Iowa's role as a pass-through corridor state; a workspace routing Midwest US freight through Iowa should treat state-level permitting and infrastructure decisions as relevant to through-traffic, not only Iowa-origin/destination shipments.

FACT: "Get Oversize & Overweight Permits IFTA (International Fuel Tax Agreement) IRP (International Registration Plan)" *Source: Iowa DOT, Freight Planning. https://iowadot.gov/transportation-development/systems-planning/areas-planning/freight

*Per the workspace's reading:* Iowa DOT operates the standard interstate trucking compliance instruments (oversize/overweight permits, IFTA fuel-tax compliance, IRP vehicle registration); these are the specific, named permit/compliance systems a workspace's Iowa-transiting or Iowa-based road-freight subcontractors need to be enrolled in.

**Industrial electricity, fuel, and labor cost baseline.**

GAP: No sourced industrial electricity, fuel, labor, port handling, or drayage cost figure for Iowa is present in the fetched source content.

# 2. Feasibility of Specific Operational Choices

FACT: "The 2025 Iowa State Rail Plan is intended to guide the Iowa Department of Transportation in its activities of promoting access to rail transportation, helping to improve the freight railroad transportation system, expanding passenger rail service, and promoting improved safety both on the rail system and where the rail system interacts with people and other transportation modes." *Source: 2025 Iowa State Rail Plan, Iowa DOT. https://iowadot.gov/transportation-development/systems-planning/areas-planning/transportation-plans/rail-plan

*Operational implication:* the 2025 Iowa State Rail Plan's own stated purpose (promoting rail access, improving the freight rail system) signals continued state-level policy support for rail as a freight mode in Iowa; a workspace with Iowa-origin or Iowa-transiting bulk or intermodal freight should treat rail as an actively supported, not declining, modal option in this state.

GAP: No verbatim regulatory or permit verdict (possible/restricted/prohibited) for a specific operational choice (on-site solar, BESS, or fleet electrification) at an Iowa logistics facility is present in the fetched source content.

# 3. Cost Comparison Against Alternatives

# 4. Cross-Regional Strategic Implications

*No content for this section as of 2026-09-17: Cross-Regional Strategic Implications is a MATRIX-then-transitive comparison requiring the same cost or feasibility dimension sourced across at least two of the workspace's active regions. This record's stored pool covers only Iowa; no other regional_data item's sourced figures were supplied for this authoring pass, so no cross-regional comparison can be proven from this single stored pool. This omission will resolve once a second active region reaches sourced coverage on the same cost/feasibility dimensions.*

# 5. Competitive Positioning in the Region

FACT: "Ryan Nonnemaker Director of U.S. Government Affairs, CPKC Railroad Mike Norris Vice-Chairman, Mid-America Port Commission Kelli O'Brien Director of Public Affairs for IA, MN, and WI, Union Pacific Railroad Joe Parsons Chief Operating Officer, Iowa Interstate Railroad" *Source: Iowa Freight Advisory Council membership, Iowa DOT. https://iowadot.gov/transportation-development/systems-planning/areas-planning/freight/freight-advisory-council

FACT: "Frank Huseman Operations Manager, NEW Cooperative/Port of Blencoe" *Source: Iowa Freight Advisory Council membership, Iowa DOT. https://iowadot.gov/transportation-development/systems-planning/areas-planning/freight/freight-advisory-council

*Analytical inference:* CPKC Railroad, Union Pacific Railroad, Iowa Interstate Railroad, the Mid-America Port Commission, and NEW Cooperative/Port of Blencoe all hold seats on the state's own Freight Advisory Council; this is a name-checkable list of the rail carriers and multimodal facility operators with formal standing in Iowa freight policy, relevant background for a workspace evaluating which Iowa rail or port partners are institutionally engaged with the state.

FACT: "Members representing the agriculture, energy, distribution, logistics, and multimodal transportation industries, as well as local and state government agencies" *Source: Iowa Freight Advisory Council, Iowa DOT. https://iowadot.gov/transportation-development/systems-planning/areas-planning/freight/freight-advisory-council

# 6. Client Conversation Talking Points

**What the workspace can credibly say:**

- *Per the workspace's reading:* Iowa's State Freight Plan (formally approved in 2022, dates quoted in Section 7) is under a public-comment-stage draft update (date quoted in Section 7), and the state's Freight Advisory Council, meeting quarterly, includes CPKC Railroad, Union Pacific Railroad, and Iowa Interstate Railroad among its rail-carrier members -- this is current, checkable evidence of active state-level freight-policy engagement in Iowa.
- *Per the workspace's reading:* Iowa's own 2025 State Rail Plan is intended to promote rail access and improve the freight rail system, evidence the state continues to support rail as a freight mode.

**What the workspace should not claim without verification:**

- Do not cite a specific Iowa industrial electricity, fuel, labor, port-handling, or drayage cost figure; none is available from the captured pool.
- Do not present a specific verdict on whether on-site solar, BESS, or fleet electrification is permitted at an Iowa logistics facility; the captured pool gives no such regulatory determination.

**Questions the workspace can pose to clients:**

- "For freight simply transiting Iowa rather than originating or terminating there, has your carrier confirmed current IFTA and IRP compliance status, given Iowa DOT's role as the state permitting authority?"

*Analytical inference:* these talking points draw only on the FACT and GAP claims already established in Sections 1, 2, and 5 above; no new fact is introduced in this section.

# 7. Pending Changes That Shift the Calculus

### MONITORING

FACT: "AMES, Iowa – Feb. 24, 2026 – The Iowa Department of Transportation (DOT) is encouraging the public, freight industry and multimodal transportation representatives, and other interested stakeholders to review and provide comments regarding the draft State Freight Plan." *Source: Iowa DOT news release, "Iowa DOT invites comments on draft State Freight Plan." https://iowadot.gov/news/2026-02-24/iowa-dot-invites-comments-draft-state-freight-plan

*Operational implication:* the draft State Freight Plan update, open for public comment as of the date quoted above, is the workspace's near-term opportunity to review or respond to Iowa's freight-policy direction before the plan is finalised; the workspace's next monitoring pass should check whether the draft has been formally adopted.

FACT: "The final State Freight Plan was presented for information to the Iowa Transportation Commission on May 10, 2022 and then forwarded to the Federal Highway Administration for approval." *Source: Iowa DOT, Freight Plan page. https://iowadot.gov/transportation-development/systems-planning/areas-planning/transportation-plans/freight-plan

FACT: "The plan was formally approved on August 18, 2022." *Source: Iowa DOT, Freight Plan page. https://iowadot.gov/transportation-development/systems-planning/areas-planning/transportation-plans/freight-plan

FACT: "The FHWA monitors and approves all State Freight Plan updates to ensure compliance with current federal surface transportation laws." *Source: Iowa DOT, Freight Plan page. https://iowadot.gov/transportation-development/systems-planning/areas-planning/transportation-plans/freight-plan

FACT: "The State Freight Plan is one of a variety of additional plans and tools the department utilizes to ultimately inform the development of the Five-Year Program." *Source: Iowa DOT, Freight Plan page. https://iowadot.gov/transportation-development/systems-planning/areas-planning/transportation-plans/freight-plan

FACT: "Recent Federal Transportation Reauthorization Acts have placed increasing emphasis on the importance of the efficient movement of freight and encourage States to consider fright movements in their overall planning processes." *Source: Iowa DOT, Freight Planning. https://iowadot.gov/transportation-development/systems-planning/areas-planning/freight

FACT: "This group was created in 2012 as a forum to assist with understanding the complexities associated with freight movements through education, discussion, and review." *Source: Iowa Freight Advisory Council, Iowa DOT. https://iowadot.gov/transportation-development/systems-planning/areas-planning/freight/freight-advisory-council

FACT: "meet on a quarterly basis to address critical topics cooperatively identified by the FAC Chair and Iowa DOT staff." *Source: Iowa Freight Advisory Council, Iowa DOT. https://iowadot.gov/transportation-development/systems-planning/areas-planning/freight/freight-advisory-council

- 2012: the Iowa Freight Advisory Council was created.
- May 10, 2022: the final State Freight Plan was presented to the Iowa Transportation Commission before forwarding to the FHWA for approval.
- August 18, 2022: the State Freight Plan was formally approved.
- Feb. 24, 2026: the Iowa DOT opened public comment on a draft State Freight Plan update.
